subject: PIT Histogram is NOT uniformly distributed

messages.author: 6c671cef0791de00
messages.subject: PIT Histogram is NOT uniformly distributed
parts:
Hi.  I am fitting a very basic spatio-temporal model (classical parametric formulation introduced by Bernardinelli et al. 1995), with an overall intercept, unstructured and structured spatial random random effects, fixed effect of time (linear), plus a differential trend (identifying the interaction between space and time).  My associated PIT histogram is not uniform and significantly skewed to the left.  What does this mean exactly?

Below is my code for the formula and the model:
formula.ST1 <- off ~ 1 + f(ID.area,model="besag",graph=Seattle.adj) + f(ID.area1,year,model="iid") + f(ID.year,model="iid") + year
model.inla.ST1 <- inla(formula.ST1,family="poisson", E = E.off, data=data, control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE), control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE), verbose = T, control.inla=list(strategy="laplace"))

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] PIT Histogram is NOT uniformly distributed
parts:
On Tue, 2014-03-18 at 12:28 -0700, lpt wrote:
> Hi. I am fitting a very basic spatio-temporal model (classical
> parametric formulation introduced by Bernardinelli et al. 1995), with
> an overall intercept, unstructured and structured spatial random
> random effects, fixed effect of time (linear), plus a differential
> trend (identifying the interaction between space and time). My
> associated PIT histogram is not uniform and significantly skewed to
> the left. What does this mean exactly?

the PIT histogram would be (close to) uniform for a perfect model. It
could also be that with a wrong model. In most cases, there are some
systematic error, like in the example below:




n = 1000
x = runif(n)
y = 1 + x + rnorm(n, sd=0.1)
r = inla(y ~ 1 + x, data = data.frame(y, x),
control.compute=list(cpo=TRUE))
hist(r$cpo$pit,n=100)

inla.dev.new()
rr = inla(y ~ -1 + I(x^2), data = data.frame(y, x),
control.compute=list(cpo=TRUE))
hist(rr$cpo$pit,n=100)
